packages.label: רֹאשׁ — הַצַּדִּיק, רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה, וְהַמֹּחַ
packages.label_en: The Head — the Tzaddik, Rosh Hashanah, and the Mind
packages.reason: All five nodes in this Torah share the same essential quality of 'ראש' (head/beginning/summit). The Tzaddik is explicitly called a bechina of ראש because he is ראש בני ישראל; Rosh Hashanah is a bechina of ראש because it is the beginning of the year; and the person's mind and da'at (מחו ודעתו) brought to the Tzaddik is a bechina of ראש because it resides in the head. The teaching's entire point is that these three ראשים converge when one travels to the Tzaddik on Rosh Hashanah. They are not cause and effect — they are three parallel expressions of the same essential quality of 'ראשיות' (headship/primacy). ראש בני ישראל is an epithet of הצדיק, naming the specific dimension in which he is a ראש.
